facts.statement: The holotype of Elemgasem was discovered in 2002 in the Sierra del Portezuelo locality of Argentina, approximately 20 km west of Cutral Có.
facts.quote: The Elemgasem holotype specimen, MCF-PVPH-380, was discovered in 2002 in layers of the Sierra del Portezuelo locality of the Portezuelo Formation, about 20 km west of Cutral Có, Neuquén Province, Argentina.

facts.statement: Elemgasem is a small abelisaurid dinosaur with an estimated body length of 3.58 meters.
facts.quote: Elemgasem is a small abelisaurid with an estimated body length of 3.58 m.

facts.statement: The holotype tail vertebrae show spondyloarthropathy, marking the first recorded case of this vertebral joint disease in a non-tetanuran theropod and the second in any non-avian theropod.
facts.quote: The holotype tail vertebrae of Elemgasem demonstrate spondyloarthropathy (vertebral joint disease), representing the first case this has been observed in a non-tetanuran theropod, and the second case in a non-avian theropod.

facts.statement: Elemgasem lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 90 to 88 million years ago (Turonian to Coniacian stages), in what is now South America.
facts.quote: Esta especie vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 90 a 88 millones de años, durante el Turoniense al Coniaciense, en lo que es hoy Sudamérica.

facts.statement: The exact position of Elemgasem within Brachyrostra is debated, with analyses placing it either as a sister taxon to Furileusauria or in various positions within that clade.
facts.quote: The cladistic position of Elemgasem within Brachyrostra is uncertain, given that phylogenetic analyses recover it as either a sister taxon to Furileusauria or in several positions within this clade.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists Furileusauria as the parent group for Elemgasem.
Elemgasem lived between 93.9 and 85.7 million years ago, spanning the Turonian to Coniacian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Coniacian (93.9 to 85.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: The holotype specimen includes partial axial and appendicular elements such as cervical and caudal vertebrae, femur, tibia, fibula, astragalus-calcaneum, metatarsals, and pedal phalanges.
facts.quote: The holotype consists of partial axial and appendicular elements, including cervical and caudal vertebrae, right femur, left tibia, right and left fibula, left astragalus-calcaneum, metatarsals, and various pedal phalanges.

facts.statement: The abelisaurid family dominated the carnivorous fauna of Gondwana during the Late Cretaceous, between 100 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: La familia Abelisauridae de dinosaurios predominó en la fauna carnívora durante el Cretácico superior, entre 100 y 66 millones de años atrás, en Gondwana, un continente formado por lo que ahora es América del Sur, la Antártida, India, África y Australia.
